## Measurement REFUTES the premise — the named metrics are publishing

AWS alarm sweep, read-only, all 17 enabled regions of account `896586841071` (only `us-east-1` holds alarms; 48 metric alarms enumerated without error).

This ticket claims the `rebar/host` alarms are inert because their metrics are not publishing. That is **no longer true**. All three are live as of `2026-09-20T10:19:00-07:00`:

| Metric | Latest value | Alarm | State | Threshold | Missing-data |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disk_used_percent{InstanceId=i-00880b2c7f13527c5,mount=/var/gerrit}` | `31.0` (33 datapoints in 3h) | `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` | OK | `>=85` | breaching |
| `gerrit_healthy{InstanceId=i-00880b2c7f13527c5}` | `1.0` | `rebar-gerrit-healthy-down` | OK | `<1` | breaching |
| `reviewbot_healthy{InstanceId=i-00880b2c7f13527c5}` | `1.0` | `rebar-reviewbot-healthy-down` | OK | `<1` | breaching |

A full scan found **no `rebar/host` alarm-backed metric with zero datapoints in the last 14 days**.

All three alarms are configured `TreatMissingData=breaching`, so had publishing genuinely stopped they would have latched into ALARM rather than sitting inert — which is itself evidence against the original reading.

**This looks like a `not_a_bug` close on refuted premise.** Leaving the disposition to you rather than closing it myself, since this ticket was explicitly parked for your decision.

**Not established:** regions EC2 reports as `not-opted-in` were not enumerated for alarms. Enabled-region enumeration completed cleanly.
